demand_phase.ceo_summary: We are delivering a lean, high-performance Win32 native application that demonstrates core system integration without the overhead of modern frameworks.
constraints: Must use RegisterClassEx, CreateWindowEx, and standard message loop.
Must link against user32 and gdi32.
Directory structure: include/CounterApp.hpp, src/CounterApp.cpp, src/main.cpp, root CMakeLists.txt.
CMakeLists.txt must set C++20 and target_include_directories for include/.
Left-click in client area must increment an integer counter displayed in the window.
demand_phase.cpo_summary: The code will be strictly organized with PascalCase headers and a clean separation of concerns between the window logic and the entry point.
demand_phase.rationale: The brief explicitly requests a Win32 C++20 application with a graphical window, message loop, and direct OS API usage (user32, gdi32), which defines the desktop_app modality.

stack_phase.build_notes: CMake 3.15+; C++20 standard; target_include_directories for include/; link user32 and gdi32; no tests; Windows Release build via build.bat
stack_phase.cto_summary: Geoff confirms the VRAM governor is stable for this lightweight Win32 workload, allowing full C++20 optimization without memory pressure.
risks: LSP verification timeouts on shadow includes (Vrammonitor.hpp) may delay CI feedback
Win32 message loop must correctly handle WM_PAINT to reflect counter state without flicker
PascalCase header naming must be strictly enforced to avoid shadow guard failures

user_brief: Create a minimal Win32 C++20 desktop app CounterApp. One window shows an integer click counter; left-click in the client area increments it. Use WinMain, RegisterClassEx, CreateWindowEx, and a standard message loop (user32, gdi32). Layout: include/CounterApp.hpp, src/CounterApp.cpp, src/main.cpp, root CMakeLists.txt (C++20, target_include_directories for include/). PascalCase headers. No tests. Self-contained.
